questions.explanation: Oxygen is the terminal electron acceptor. It accepts electrons and protons to form water, and this final acceptance permits electron flow through the aerobic electron transport chain to continue normally. [ev_resp02_terminal_acceptor, ev_resp02_accepts_electrons, ev_resp02_forms_water, ev_resp02_flow_continues]

options.text: Oxygen is the terminal electron acceptor; it accepts electrons and protons to form water, allowing the aerobic-chain electron flow to continue.
Oxygen is an upstream electron acceptor; it accepts electrons and protons to form water, allowing the aerobic-chain electron flow to continue.
Oxygen is the terminal electron acceptor; it releases electrons and protons to form water, allowing the aerobic-chain electron flow to continue.
Oxygen is the terminal electron acceptor; it accepts electrons and protons to form carbon dioxide, allowing the aerobic-chain electron flow to continue.
